messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@orbithealth.com>, Maya Torres <maya@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit Health - follow-up: usage & invoice estimate

Hi Rajiv / Maya,

Great to meet you both on the call earlier - thanks for walking us through Orbit Health's ingestion and query patterns. Quick recap and the next steps so we can put together a clean invoice estimate: 

Recap (as I heard it):
- Production traffic: ~45M tokens/month of embedding generation (batching from nightly jobs) and ~15M tokens/month of streaming text generation across interactive UIs.
- Peak concurrency: small bursty queries from clinicians during morning standup (up to 20 concurrent streams).
- Retention & security: data stored in your VPC; you mentioned SOC 2 in-scope and need for customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Target unit economics: your finance team is aiming for an infra spend of ~$800-1,200 per 1M tokens on peak LLM calls (you noted that number might be negotiable if we can improve batching/kv cache).

Ask for confirmation so we can finalize the estimate:
1) Can you confirm monthly token volumes (embedding vs generation) and a +/- 20% range for Q3?
2) Is the $/1M target a hard ceiling or a target range?
3) Any procurement constraints (PO timing, required contract terms, who owns billing)?

I attached a copy of your pricing model worksheet we used during the call (orbit_pricing_model_v2.xlsx) and will drop a PDF invoice estimate once we align on final volumes.

Next steps:
- You: confirm volumes and budget range (1-2 business days)
- Me: produce a line-item invoice estimate + cost breakdown (same day after volumes confirmed)
- Quick follow-up call if helpful - I can do 30 minutes tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Sean
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: orbit_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@orbithealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbit Health - follow-up: usage & invoice estimate

Thanks Sean - solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly volumes (current / expected):
  - Embeddings: 42M tokens/month (expected +10% in Q3: 46.2M)
  - Generation (user queries): 14M tokens/month (expected stable within +/-15%)
- Budget range: finance said they can approve up to $1,000 per 1M tokens for Q3 pilot, but would prefer closer to $800 if demonstrated cost-savings via batching/caching.
- Procurement: we need a standard SOW and PO; billing will be handled by our procurement team (cc'd soon).

I've uploaded an Orbit internal worksheet with the projected monthly ranges to the drive folder - link in the email from earlier. For now, confirm if you can provide both a conservative estimate (no batching improvements) and an optimized estimate (with batching + KV cache enabled) so our CFO can see the delta.

--Rajiv
Head of Data Products | Orbit Health
rajiv@orbithealth.com

Rajiv - thanks for the quick confirmation and the ranges, that helps a lot. Attached is a preliminary invoice estimate and a short cost-model summary (redwood_invoice_estimate.pdf). High-level numbers below so it's easy to share with finance: 

Conservative (no additional batching/caching improvements) - monthly:
- Embeddings: 46.2M tokens @ $0.45 per 1k tokens = $20,790
- Generation: 14M tokens @ $2.50 per 1k tokens = $35,000
- Infrastructure / reserved capacity amortized = $4,500
- Estimated monthly total = $60,290
- Implied $/1M tokens (combined)  $1,062

Optimized (batching + KV cache + quantized runtime) - monthly:
- Embeddings: 46.2M tokens effective cost reduced by 40% = $12,474
- Generation: 14M tokens effective cost reduced by 30% = $24,500
- Infrastructure / reserved capacity amortized = $4,000
- Estimated monthly total = $41,0..74 (wait, typo)

(please ignore the stray characters - corrected numbers attached)

What I did:
- Used your provided volumes in orbit_pricing_model_v2.xlsx and applied Redwood standard price tiers + a pilot discount for Q3.
- Included a line for reserved capacity (if you prefer pay-as-you-go we can show that alternative; it shifts unit economics slightly).

Next: I'm going to correct that small formatting error and upload a clean PDF with both scenarios broken down per line-item and per 1M-token unit economics. Would you like me to also include a 12-month pro forma?

If helpful we can lock a 30-minute slot tomorrow (June 30) to walk through the PDF with your procurement team - suggest 10:30am PT.

Thanks,
Sean
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
